reviews.comment: The lectures are boring and lengthy. Be sure the TA is good! That's the only way you will do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The TA is the only hope you have for this class. Prof's lectures are so unorganized and scattered that you don't even know what he's talking about in lecture. Its doable if you have no other option but not recommended whatsoever.

Easy A if you do well on the weekly quizzes. If you want to do well go to the TA after every class! I could not recommend this enough. Without the TA, the quizzes would have been a little hard. His lectures are pretty bland so I would suggest to go for the attendance. You'll learn everything you need from the TA and Jeff Hansen.

Little has bland lectures and is slow. His grading system with quizzes can be frustrating but it's pretty fair. Our tests were open notes and some of the problems were copy paste from the lecture, so they were free points. You may not learn a ton, but he does know what he's talking about, and he grades easy enough that you can get an A if you try.

Monotone and boring lectures. He expects you to already know a lot of the content. His slides had lots of mistakes and won't respond to emails and doesn't really answer questions in class. He gave a little extra credit at the end of the semester. The TA seemed to do the grading and he was really nice. Weekly quizzes are hard and 40% of your grade.

Prof's lectures were extremely unengaging, monotone, and so boring. Prof is generous, knowledgeable, and a nice person. Course content is complicated and too large of a scope; this class feels like a "learn what you can, you won't understand it all" type of class. Most of my learning came from the TA's explaining the labs.

His lectures are pretty boring, you're better off watching Jeff Hanson's vid on YouTube. He doesn't really communicate the expectations or info about tests. Will never answer emails or update the canvas page. You can definitely make an A, but you won't learn much.

He is a great professor, his lectures might put you to sleep a little, but it is obvious he is very knowledgeable about mechanics of materials and that he cares about the students. His exam's are fairly easy and usually based on his slides. His TA was probably the most helpful TA I've had.

Hes really lenient with how he grades. He made some of the quizzes take home near the end and gave people who didnt submit homework at all the opportunity to do it late at the end of the semester. He also gave us 10 free points before on the final just because. In terms of teaching hes pretty average, but hes definitely a nice guy who cares.

Dallas Little is a very nice guy. It seems like he actually cares about his students when you talk to him, but man, this guy honestly has the driest lectures. His voice is very monotone. The good thing about this class is that its centered more around weekly quizzes instead of midterms. Not saying its easy, but less opportunity to fail. Do the HW
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Go to class, listen and take notes very well, study a lot, be smart on the tests and do all the labs and you'll do fine. Don't and you won't. Really hard class, Mr Little walks in, gives an almost robotic lecture and walks out. Everything else is handled by the TA. Our TA was amazing, that really saved us as a class.

Lectures are all over the place and it's almost impossible to determine what's actually important for tests. Tests are multiple choice, but all the answers are almost the same. Just hope you have a good TA to make it bearable.

Do not take this professor. He does not teach well enough for you to take his tests. Studying will hardly do you any good. Rely on the curve. The class is homework heavy, but you at least get to submit it with a group. He gave one of my friend's a final grade of an A, but discovered something "wrong" on her final, then he gave her a B instead.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES
